newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Communists call for referendum on euro.
newsitem.headline: French Communists call for referendum on euro.

text.p: France's Communists launched a campaign for a referendum on the European single currency on Thursday, saying that they had already gathered 100,000 of an expected one million signatures.

The Communist Party daily L'Humanite published a full-page petition for readers to pass around and send to President Jacques Chirac, demanding that he ask voters whether they want France to join the single currency.

A CSA opinion poll published at the weekend by L'Humanite said two-thirds of voters favoured calling a referendum. It said a 61 to 39 percent majority wanted France to join, but 68 percent believed they were ill-informed about the euro.

France narrowly passed the European monetary union in a 1992 referendum. Chirac said during his presidential election campaign in 1994 that he favoured calling another referendum, but he has since rowed back.
The Communists, who oppose the single currency, have made a referendum a condition of a left-wing alliance with the Socialists in a 1998 general election. The Socialists oppose calling a referendum.
